slides.title: Stairs, stairs, stairs
slides.text: Bolt has to climb three stairs that all look the same. Building every stair block by block takes forever.
slides.alt: Three gem steps climb like stairs to the flag, and Bolt's program tray is empty: climbing all three the long way takes a lot of blocks.

focus.cue: Three gem steps climb like stairs to the flag.
The tray is empty: every step longhand takes forever.

slides.title: Make your own block
slides.text: A My Block is a group of steps with a name, like Stair. Make it once. Then a call block runs the whole group wherever you put it.
slides.alt: The My Block named Stair is built in the tray: move, pick up, turn right, move, turn left: one named packet of blocks.

focus.cue: The new block has a name: Stair.
Inside it: the five steps of one stair, packed together.

slides.title: Climb three stairs
slides.text: The Stair block holds the steps for one stair. Three calls climb all three stairs.
slides.alt: The Stair block is defined once, then called three times in a row at the bottom of the tray: call Stair, call Stair, call Stair.

focus.cue: Stair is made once, up here.
Three calls at the bottom climb all three stairs.

slides.title: Nothing happens until you call
slides.text: Making a My Block does nothing by itself. Bolt only does its steps when a call block is in the program.
slides.alt: The My Block named Side is defined in the tray, but nothing calls it, and Bolt has not moved: a definition alone does nothing.

focus.cue: Side is made — but look below it: no call anywhere.
So Bolt has not moved at all.

slides.title: Remix and give credit
slides.text: You may change a block someone else made. That is a remix. Keep the line that says where it came from, so everyone knows who started it.
slides.alt: Two My Blocks named Zig sit in the tray, and the second carries a based-on Starter blocks stamp: a remix keeps its credit.

focus.cue: Zig carries a stamp: based on Starter blocks.
The remix keeps the credit line too.

words.means: a group of steps you name once and use again
the block that runs a My Block
the name programmers use for a named group of steps
changing something someone else made and giving them credit

slides.title: Bolt's piece lights up
slides.text: Bolt's piece of the Spark is lit — the first of four. His roads are only the start: next comes the Bug Hunters trail, where Bolt learns to hunt for mistakes.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Functions and finish all 6 levels, including the one where you remix a starter block. Split each route into named parts first.
slides.alt: Three gem steps climb like stairs to the flag, and Bolt's program tray is empty: climbing all three the long way takes a lot of blocks.

focus.cue: Your turn: split the climb into named parts first.
